title: What Happens When You Sweat?
description:
Send this to the friend who sniff-checks their armpit after the gym.
You have 2 to 4 million eccrine sweat glands, packed tightest on your palms and soles, and their sweat is about 99% water with a little salt that cools you as it evaporates. Fresh sweat itself has no smell: the odor starts when bacteria on your skin break it down, mostly the thicker 'stress sweat' from apocrine glands in your armpits (Cleveland Clinic). A sudden change in body odor or sweating is worth a talk with a doctor (Cleveland Clinic); hot skin that has stopped sweating plus confusion can mean heatstroke, an emergency (NHS).
Next Body File: why your nose runs in the cold.
Follow Body Files for a new one every day.

structure_note: Sniff-test reveal: one sweat drop followed from gland to smell. Beat 1: extreme close-up of a single fresh sweat drop on the hero's forearm mid-workout, a cartoon nose hovering over it, pills 'A STINKS' / 'B SMELLS OF NOTHING' and a tiny tag 'UP TO 4 MILLION GLANDS'. Beat 2: x-ray cyan skin cross-section, coiled glands pumping salty water up a duct; the drop evaporates into wavy heat lines (cooling). Beat 3: heat-map of the body, palms and soles glowing densest. Relatable: hero at a job-interview desk, palms shining. Re-hook: hard cut and zoom into the armpit, a second, bigger gland type wakes up and oozes a thicker, stickier drop. Then bacteria characters swarm and munch the drop; green stink lines appear only after they bite. Reveal: pill B gets the check. Safety: calm card, a thermometer and dry skin icon, phone icon. Tease: hero outside in cold air, breath fog, a drip at the nose tip, then cut back to frame 1's sweat drop close-up. Distinct from the last videos: no doorway, no scan, no diary, no lineup, no showdown, no nerve map.
safety: Curious-friend tone, no personal medical advice, no deodorant or product advice. Voiced safety line uses NHS heatstroke signs ('hot skin that's not sweating', 'confused' -> 'Call 999') phrased as 'Call emergency services' for the US audience. Cleveland Clinic 'sudden change in body odor or sweating' pointer is in the description only. Dropped or not voiced: '4 liters of sweat per hour' (true per Cleveland Clinic Eccrine Glands but an extreme-sounding number that invites challenge framing), specific bacteria species (not on Cleveland Clinic pages), fruity-odor/diabetes link (cut for length and scare risk).
